name: twin-v0
title: A whole AWS in one page: the twin v0
presenter: synthetic, cast by studio.c, labelled synthetic; AI voice, disclosed; subtitles always on

quote.text: the code either hits the AWS from the browser ... or it hits the twin, but the code should not know the difference
quote.show: on-screen text only, beat b7, never spoken in his voice

beats.narration: What if you could try an AWS console without an AWS account? I am a synthetic presenter, for a synthetic AWS.

visual.alt: The hub, signed out: the hero and the Try the twin button

beats.narration: One button, and this page talks to a twin of AWS that runs inside your browser.

visual.alt: Twin mode on: the bar says a synthetic AWS runs in this page, account id masked

beats.narration: Same read role, same one-hour credentials, same calls. Even the account number is made up.

visual.alt: The twin account: read role, credentials until one hour on; account id and the synthetic cost masked

beats.narration: The calls are signed just as AWS expects them, and the twin answers in the same formats.

visual.alt: S3 browser: five buckets listed; the account id in their names masked

beats.narration: Zips open right in the page, with every file inside listed. Big ones are read from their index, not downloaded whole.

visual.alt: A Lambda dependencies zip opened: four files inside (this small one read whole, as the page says)

beats.narration: Compressed logs open right here too, unpacked and shown as formatted JSON, in the page.

visual.alt: A CloudFront log, .gz, unzipped in the browser and shown as formatted JSON

beats.narration: The same code talks to your real AWS when you sign in. It is open source, at aws dot platform dot sovereignweb dot site.

visual.alt: Back on the hub after leaving the twin; quote as on-screen text, then the address
